markdown_report:
**Select normalized recency weighting for the corrected GRU4Rec.** At 10% research progress, this offers a small, controlled intervention with unchanged inference.

Three insights follow from the supplied evidence. First, deleting recent items changes sampled training ranks more than deleting oldest items, motivating a recency hypothesis without establishing benefit. Second, older-item shuffling also changes ranks, so older context should remain available. Third, strong sampled training margins do not establish validation accuracy; neither margins nor qualitative feedback identifies an optimal decay.

Three literature insights constrain the experiment. Recency Sampling [1] directly motivates emphasizing recent supervision in sequential recommenders, but does not establish this weighting rule. RNN gradient analysis [2] distinguishes recurrent memory attenuation from weighting training targets; changing one does not repair the other. Sampled-metric analysis [3] shows why diagnostic rankings cannot substitute for the pinned benchmark.

These insights organize three directions: supervision allocation, recurrent credit assignment, and evaluation reliability. Their conceptual map is:

| Direction | Intervention | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision | Reweight recent target losses | Validate decay experimentally |
| Credit assignment | Preserve complete causal GRU computation | Sensitivity does not establish usefulness |
| Reliability | Retain evaluator and verify predictor parity | Module checks alone omit routing |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; greater difficulty means more engineering.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Normalized exponential loss weights [1] | 3/7/2 | Originality: precise controlled adaptation, established principle. Potential: cheap transferable ablation, uncertain gains. Difficulty: simple tensor reduction, baseline reduction needs verification. |
| Uniform-to-recency training schedule [1] | 4/6/3 | Originality: combines curriculum and recency, familiar ingredients. Potential: retains early broad supervision, adds schedule uncertainty. Difficulty: one epoch-dependent scalar, another comparison consumes budget. |
| Lag-stratified gradient alignment [2] | 3/6/5 | Originality: task-specific analysis, established gradient tools. Potential: distinguishes conflicting supervision, local gradients cannot predict generalization. Difficulty: no inference changes, costly separate backward passes. |

For the selected idea, assign each valid target an age relative to the newest valid target in its training window. Use weights from 0.25 at the oldest target to 1 at the newest, then normalize within each row to mean one. This preserves each row’s total supervision weight under a global valid-position mean while changing its temporal allocation. Single-target rows retain weight one. Preserve every causal input and sampled negative.

Compare against uniform weighting with all other settings fixed. Train one model per category; select solely through unchanged macro validation HR@10. Preserve seeds, routing, diagnostic interfaces and execution limits. This remains a hypothesis: stronger recency may discard useful supervision, and feedback about compatibility cannot supply missing compatibility labels.

References: [1] [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643); [2] [RNN training difficulties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.5063); [3] [On Sampled Metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

idea.description: Apply row-normalized exponential window-relative recency weights to unreduced causal next-item losses in the supplied corrected GRU4Rec. Preserve its backbone, sampler, optimizer, causal inputs and inference scores. Train exactly one independent model per category.
idea.motivation: Recent-history deletion produces larger diagnostic rank changes than oldest-history deletion, while older-order perturbations remain consequential. This supports testing a gentle redistribution of supervision while retaining all history. It does not establish that existing recency reliance is insufficient or that weighting will improve validation HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate the supplied reducer after computing the baseline's unreduced per-position loss, including all baseline positive/negative terms. Do not replace the objective or sampler. The code explicitly supports global valid-position mean or sum reduction; select the baseline's actual reduction. If it instead uses sequence-balanced reduction or separately normalized terms, preserve those semantics with an equivalent adapter before running the comparison. Baseline source was not supplied, so reduction compatibility is not verified here.

Use alpha=log(4) for the primary experiment and alpha=0 for its uniform control, with the same setting across all four categories. Weights depend only on valid supervision positions within the sampled training window. They never enter the recurrent input or inference. Normalizing within rows preserves their total weight under either supported reduction; it does not equalize rows of different lengths. Add unchanged baseline regularization after the data-loss reduction. Log valid-target counts and per-row weight ESS=(sum w)^2/sum(w^2), explicitly describing ESS as concentration rather than independent sample count. Skip optimizer updates on batches without valid supervision.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl; DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and artifacts stay beneath the current trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, 200 batches per epoch and at most 200 epochs. All training and diagnostics count against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not reuse other-trial checkpoints, average checkpoints, fuse scores or introduce fitted auxiliary predictors. Preserve baseline checkpoint selection and use only the unchanged host validation evaluator for comparison; no improvement is claimed here.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView hooks, with the actual trained nn.Module exposed as view.model. Preserve B x L feature alignment, public loader yields, and measured metric definitions. Unavailable attributes remain unavailable. idea.pseudocode:
import math
import torch


def recency_weighted_loss(position_loss, sequence, positive, negative,
                         alpha=math.log(4.0), reduction='mean'):
    """Reduce the existing GRU4Rec per-position objective.

    All inputs have shape B x L. position_loss must already contain
    the unchanged baseline objective's terms, without regularization.
    Validity here assumes the baseline requires a nonzero negative.
    Preserve its actual validity mask if its objective differs.
    Returns (loss_or_None, detached_diagnostics).
    """
    if reduction not in ('mean', 'sum'):
        raise ValueError('Adapt explicitly to the baseline reduction')
    if not math.isfinite(alpha) or alpha < 0:
        raise ValueError('alpha must be finite and nonnegative')
    if not (position_loss.shape == sequence.shape == positive.shape
            == negative.shape):
        raise ValueError('Expected aligned B x L tensors')

    valid = sequence.ne(0) & positive.ne(0) & negative.ne(0)
    count = valid.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    if not bool(valid.any()):
        return None, {'valid_positions': 0, 'ess_per_row': []}
    if not bool(torch.isfinite(position_loss[valid]).all()):
        raise FloatingPointError('Nonfinite valid baseline losses')

    # Rank only supervised positions; left-padding width has no effect.
    ordinal = valid.long().cumsum(dim=1) - 1
    relative_age = (count - 1 - ordinal).float()
    relative_age = relative_age / (count - 1).clamp_min(1).float()
    relative_age = torch.where(valid, relative_age,
                               torch.zeros_like(relative_age))
    raw = torch.exp(-alpha * relative_age) * valid.float()
    mass = raw.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    weights = raw * count.float() / mass.clamp_min(1e-12)

    safe_loss = torch.where(valid, position_loss.float(),
                            torch.zeros_like(position_loss, dtype=torch.float32))
    total = (weights * safe_loss).sum()
    loss = total / valid.sum() if reduction == 'mean' else total

    ess = mass.square() / raw.square().sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
    diagnostics = {
        'valid_positions': int(valid.sum().item()),
        'ess_per_row': ess[count.ne(0)].detach().cpu().tolist(),
    }
    return loss, diagnostics

originality.positive: Row normalization makes the temporal intervention explicit while preserving each row's total supervision weight under the declared reduction.
originality.negative: Recency-biased supervision and exponential weighting are established techniques; this is a controlled adaptation.

future_potential.positive: A cheap experiment can clarify whether supervision allocation improves the fixed four-category recurrent benchmark.
future_potential.negative: Existing temporal reliance may already suffice, and reduced emphasis on older targets could hurt generalization.

code_difficulty.positive: The intervention uses standard tensor operations without changing architecture, sampling or inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct integration requires verifying the baseline's unreduced objective, validity mask and reduction.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling for Next-Item Recommendation
contributions: Provides direct precedent for recency-biased supervision in sequential recommendation, including GRU4Rec.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed normalized exponential weights or decay strength improve this pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: On the Difficulty of Training Recurrent Neural Networks
contributions: Explains recurrent gradient attenuation and instability, separating memory propagation from supervision weighting.
limitations: Does not validate recency loss weighting for recommendation or predict its validation benefit.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can produce misleading model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not replace the task's mandatory pinned sampled HR@10 selection criterion or establish unobserved preferences.
